subject: Follow-up: HealthPulse data handling — PII redaction + short log window
messages:
From: Sarah Murphy <sarah@healthpulse.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@healthpulse.com>, legal@healthpulse.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick follow-up from today's discovery (PII handling + log window)

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks for the demo and the call earlier. Two quick follow-ups from our side after discussing internally with product and legal:

1) PII scope: We need confirmation that HealthPulse patient-identifiable data can be redacted at ingestion so it is never written to persistent logs or long-lived caches. Specifically: names, national IDs, DOB, and free-text notes that match PHI patterns. The ask is effectively a 0-retention promise for PII fields.

2) Shortened operational logs: For non-PII telemetry (latency, token counts, anonymized intent tags) we can accept a 7-day retention window for observability.

3) Residency: For EU patients we prefer processing and logs to remain in the eu region (keys and KMS in EU ideally).

4) Audit evidence: Can you share SOC2 summary and a sample DPA or contract language that captures the 0-retention carveout (or an exception path)?

We are still evaluating, but if Redwood can provide the above (or a pilot path), we can move forward quickly.

Appreciate a short recap and next steps.

—Sarah
Sarah Murphy
Head of Privacy & Compliance
HealthPulse

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery (PII handling + log window)

Jasmine / Monica — quick technical confirmation and constraints below. Happy to jump on a call with HealthPulse if they want more detail.

Short answers:
- PII redaction at ingestion: feasible. We can push a filter/transform step into the ingress path that strips or tokens PII fields before they reach any durable logs. This will require HealthPulse to provide the canonical field map (which keys in payload are PII) or a small set of regex/pattern rules we can run at the edge.

- 0-retention guarantee for PII fields: operationally we can set pipeline to not write PII to persistent logs and to avoid writing PII into long-lived model KV storage. Caveat: if you enable full conversation history on the client side and then send past content back to Redwood for context, those are outside the ingestion filter unless we are inserted at the client boundary — we'll document recommended client-side redaction.

- Shortened 7-day logs for non-PII: supported via per-customer retention policy. We can configure the observability stack to auto-drop telemetry older than 7 days and ensure backups/snapshots exclude that bucket. Note: aggregated billing/token metrics would still be kept for billing reconciliation per contract (we can store aggregated monthly totals rather than per-request payloads).

- EU residency / KMS: we can pin processing to eu regions. For full key residency we require customer-managed KMS or an HSM-backed key per the Private deployment pattern; otherwise we can use Redwood-managed EU KMS with contractual assurances.

- Audit evidence: we have a SOC2 summary and redact-capable configuration artifacts. I'll attach a short SOC2 extract and a sample config JSON for the pilot (no secrets).

Pilot checklist (high level):
1) HealthPulse provides PII field map and a representative prompt/payload sample.
2) Sign DPA addendum that specifies the 0-retention carveout and the 7-day log window for telemetry.
3) Configure ingress filter in staging + run 72h shadow traffic validation.
4) Enable pilot in eu region on a single model/route, 2-week observation.

Risks / exceptions:
- Real-time KV caching: if model accuracy depends on previously seen PII in KV, removing it may affect results. We'll do side-by-side evals.
- Legal-specific exports: if HealthPulse requires full forensic logs for an investigation, that would be an exception path we need to handle contractually.

Attaching: "SOC2-summary.pdf" and "sample-config.json" (stubs).

—Rishi
